<SUMMARY>The global geopolitical landscape is marked by intensifying technological competition and ongoing regional conflicts. President Trump's administration is implementing new tariff walls and expanding sanctions on Cuba. The US-Iran conflict continues to drive energy cost inflation and supply chain disruptions, prompting Asia to turn to US oil and gas, while diplomatic efforts yield no tangible progress in ending the conflict despite President Trump's claims of a close deal. Europe is advancing its "tech sovereignty" initiative with a comprehensive package to bolster domestic semiconductor, cloud, and AI capabilities, including new photonics integration. The demand for AI chips and infrastructure is driving significant investments globally, but also highlights supply chain bottlenecks and rising energy consumption concerns in the Americas and Australia. The critical minerals sector sees increased strategic maneuvering, with the EU investing in South Africa and China tightening its grip on various resources, while US companies expand domestic rare earth processing and Brazil emerges as a significant lithium player. Geopolitical tensions include China's actions in the South China Sea and export controls on AI experts and rare earths, and Taiwan warns of AI supply chain issues. India is actively amending its semiconductor policy and collaborating with international partners for chip manufacturing. The US House of Representatives has passed a war powers resolution regarding the Iran conflict, indicating internal US policy divisions.</SUMMARY>
<EWS>The US-Iran conflict's ongoing nature, evidenced by missile and drone activity and diplomatic stalemate despite President Trump's statements, poses a persistent risk of energy price surges and global supply chain disruptions. The US Commerce Department's admitted failure to enforce AI export controls on China suggests a potential leakage of critical technology and expertise, undermining strategic objectives. Taiwan AI firms' warnings of new supply chain bottlenecks signal fragility in the burgeoning AI compute sector, while China's tightening grip on Silicon Carbide and prolonged rare-earth export curbs present significant supply chain vulnerabilities for crucial components.</EWS>
<EXEC>
**Asia:**
China has forbidden top AI experts from leaving the country without approval. China's Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) states that US export controls disrupt global semiconductor supply chains. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) maintains its central position in the AI compute supply chain and emphasizes that energy use is forcing a rethink of AI chip design. TSMC's SoIC technology is deepening AI chipmaker lock-in. Taiwan AI firms warn of new supply chain bottlenecks amid a demand boom. ROHM Semiconductor's 750V SiC MOSFET has been adopted in Battery Backup Units (BBUs) for AI server power supplies. SurplusGLOBAL has secured Korean patents for AI-powered export control automation technology, enhancing safety in semiconductor equipment and parts transactions.

**Europe:**
The European Union has launched a "tech sovereignty" package to boost chips, cloud, and AI capabilities at home, reducing reliance on American and Chinese providers. The EU Chips Act 2.0 proposal aims to shape Europe's digital future, with photonics confirmed as a new structural addition to EU policy. SK Hynix is expected to double wafer capacity globally amid an AI memory shortage, a development noted for its relevance to European supply concerns. Dutch chipmaker Nexperia, facing the loss of its China operations, plans to produce in the United States. A new EU plan seeks to enable Europe to catch up to the US and China in AI.

**Americas:**
President Donald Trump plans to rebuild the tariff wall by proposing extra tariffs of 10% or more for products from 60 major US trading partners, following an investigation into forced labor. Chuck Flint emphasizes that American prosperity depends on ending reliance on Chinese supply chains. Broadcom missed Wall Street expectations for second-quarter revenue due to increased competition in the custom semiconductor market, which impacted gains from its AI chips, causing shares to fall over 11%. Microsoft made various product announcements at its Build 2026 event, impacting the AI sector. Artificial intelligence companies in the US are warning of bottlenecks in supply chains. TSMC is tapping Nvidia's accelerated computing to drive next-generation semiconductor fabs, indicating a close partnership in advanced manufacturing.

**Oceania:**
IREN Limited has announced securing a transmission connection agreement for a planned 800MW AI data center campus in Bundey, South Australia, with energization targeted for 2028. Megaport has secured four AI deals and will raise $594 million to build an inference cloud, indicating significant investment in AI infrastructure in the region.
</EXEC>
<LITHO>
**Europe:**
The EU Chips Act 2.0 proposal has been released, confirming photonics as a new structural addition to EU policy.

**INDIA:**
Tata has partnered with ASML to advance India's chip supply chain, accelerating the country's semiconductor ambitions.
</LITHO>
<REE>
**Asia:**
China has implemented prolonged rare-earth curbs and economic retaliation against Tokyo. China has also tightened its grip on Silicon Carbide as the industry shifts to 8-inch wafers. The simultaneous wars in Ukraine and Iran have depleted tungsten sources, a metal critical for munitions and industrial production. China has asserted itself as having built the world's largest "magnet army."

**Africa:**
Indonesia's Foreign Minister Sugiono has identified Madagascar as a strategic gateway to Africa's mineral wealth, calling for deepened economic ties. The EU has pledged billions to South Africa in critical minerals investments, while China simultaneously tightens its grip on these resources. Congo has imposed cobalt export quotas to stabilize prices and attract investment.

**Europe:**
Greenland has blocked a critical rare earth project, contributing to China's tightening grip on rare earth supplies. USA Rare Earth plans additional investment in the French rare earth ecosystem. Norway reports having sufficient rare earths for Europe.

**Americas:**
USA Rare Earth has finalized a $1.6 billion deal with the US Commerce Department. USA Rare Earth has selected Cherokee County, South Carolina, for a new rare earth metal and magnet manufacturing operation. Brazil is positioned to challenge China's rare earths dominance, holding one of the largest lithium reserves globally.
</REE>
<GEO>
**Asia:**
Pakistan has emerged as a surprising ally for President Trump as the world awaits approval for a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and potentially conclude the US-Iran conflict. A US package of anti-aircraft and anti-ship missiles to Taiwan initiated a standoff. Taiwan's stock market is notably larger than India's. Japan's economic security law amendment bill is being pursued in the Senate Cabinet Committee.

**Africa:**
Washington has allowed Middle Eastern partners to expand their influence in Africa, leading to "African adventurism" by Gulf states.

**Europe:**
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is considering a three-nation tour of Europe from June 13, with visits to Britain, Italy, and France. Ireland's data processing activities account for 21% of its electricity use, prompting the UN to label it a "cautionary tale" for other nations facing data center strain. The European Commission has introduced a comprehensive legislative package designed to establish technological sovereignty and reduce the bloc's dependence on American and Chinese providers.

**Americas:**
President Trump's administration has rolled out unprecedented secondary sanctions on Cuba, targeting foreign firms doing business with the military-linked conglomerate GAESA. President Trump's administration will dismantle a $368 million monitoring system providing critical data on the world's oceans. Artificial intelligence's energy consumption is contributing to more expensive electricity, posing a problem for many. A recent survey shows a dramatic swing against new data center construction in the US. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith is seeking to forge stronger economic ties with Quebec. Bernie Sanders advocates for Americans to own a piece of AI, with the Trump White House reportedly agreeing. Peter Thiel has moved to Argentina.
</GEO>
<MILITARY>
**Asia:**
China claims it drove away a Dutch warship near the disputed Paracel Islands. A US package of anti-aircraft and anti-ship missiles to Taiwan led to a dangerous standoff with President Xi Jinping.

**Americas:**
The Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) is assessing US military options toward Cuba.
</MILITARY>
<CONCLUSION>
The technology sector remains at the forefront of geopolitical competition, with the US, EU, and China each pursuing distinct strategies for AI, chips, and critical minerals. The US is reasserting trade protectionism with new tariffs, while simultaneously investing in domestic rare earth processing and exploring quantum technologies. Europe's "tech sovereignty" push underscores a global trend towards securing domestic supply chains and reducing external dependencies in critical technology. The persistent US-Iran conflict continues to exert significant economic pressure through elevated energy costs and supply chain disruptions, impacting global markets and prompting regional energy shifts. Critical mineral supply chains are increasingly weaponized and diversified, with China's dominance being actively challenged by US and EU initiatives and emerging players like Brazil and Congo. Military tensions in the South China Sea and around Taiwan underscore ongoing flashpoints, while domestic political actions in the US reflect internal divisions regarding the Iran conflict.
</CONCLUSION>

<INDIA>
The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet has amended the Semiconductor Policy-2024 to align with the India Semiconductor Mission, aiming to boost investor flexibility, accelerate unit setup, and reduce import dependence. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has raised concerns over a Union government policy change that reclassifies laterite with over 20% aluminium as a major mineral, shifting it from state control to central auction rules. Marco Rubio's visit aimed to mend US-India ties, emphasizing strategic importance and focusing on critical minerals and underwater domain awareness. India faces economic headwinds from global events and domestic investor wariness, indicating that traditional reform models are insufficient and strategic sectors like energy and green tech require state intervention, including public investment and risk absorption. US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor met Department of Atomic Energy Secretary Dr Ajit Kumar Mohanty and congratulated him on the enactment of the SHANTI Act. Tata has partnered with ASML to advance India's chip supply chain, accelerating the country's chip manufacturing goals.</INDIA>
<WEST_ASIA>
The US-Iran conflict continues with missiles and drones flying, and Iran's foreign minister reports "no tangible progress" in talks to end the Middle East war, despite President Trump's assertion that a deal is close. Renewed hostilities included US and Iranian strikes, straining a fragile ceasefire. The conflict is driving moderate-to-strong inflation in the US, largely due to surging energy costs, with higher oil prices disrupting supply chains and lifting input costs. This energy disruption from the Iran war is jolting Asia and Europe to accelerate their energy transition efforts and is causing Asia to turn to US oil and gas. Prolonged energy disruption from the Iran war is projected to be a severe blow to the global economy. Middle East fears and AI worries are influencing market sentiment, and the AI vertical is among those most exposed to the Middle East conflict. US stocks have slipped as growing strains on the US-Iran ceasefire lifted oil prices. Washington has allowed its Middle Eastern partners to expand their influence in Africa. The Middle East and Africa data center construction market is projected to reach USD 15.97 billion by 2031. President Trump has confirmed he will attend the NATO summit in Turkey in July. President Trump confirmed calling Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu "crazy" over the phone, but stated they are "still getting along." The US House of Representatives has passed a war powers resolution directing President Trump to end hostilities with Iran, a bipartisan rebuke that is largely symbolic due to likely Senate inaction and a potential presidential veto. Israel’s war on Lebanon is escalating, with advocacy groups stating it is quickly turning southern Lebanon into the "next Gaza." Saudi Arabia's energy minister called for a "stable energy sector" during a visit to Russia.</WEST_ASIA>

<FINAL_CONCLUSION>The coming weeks will likely see continued diplomatic efforts and military posturing regarding the US-Iran conflict, with a high probability of persistent energy market volatility and supply chain pressures if a resolution remains elusive. The global race for technological supremacy, particularly in AI and advanced semiconductors, will intensify, characterized by increased nationalistic industrial policies and strategic investments across the Americas, Europe, and Asia. Further export controls and counter-measures, especially between the US and China, are anticipated in critical technology and raw materials sectors. Nations will prioritize diversifying critical mineral supply chains, leading to more bilateral agreements and investments in emerging resource-rich regions, while the energy demands of advanced computing infrastructure will increasingly influence national power policies and urban development.</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
